page: Microsoft Azure M416-208s_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MSv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 208 vCPUs mapped to 104 physical Intel Xeon 8280L cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with an exceptionally large memory capacity of 5700.0 GB, which translates to 27.4 GB per core, and includes 8389 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability. No GPUs are present in this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile characterized by weak single-core capabilities but top-tier multi-threaded and memory performance. Single-core tests, such as stress-ng single-core CPU and single-threaded gzip compression, fall into the bottom 25%. Conversely, multi-core performance is highly competitive, with stress-ng multi-core CPU, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, and Passmark CPU scores ranking in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is a primary strength, achieving top-tier status in both cached small-block reads at 10446.46 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 651.24 GB/sec.

Given the massive memory-to-vCPU ratio and high physical core count, this server offers high resource density for enterprise-scale workloads where memory capacity is the primary bottleneck. It is highly efficient for running large in-memory databases, as demonstrated by its top-tier Redis SET performance of 162.62 million operations per second. The server is also well-suited for heavy multi-threaded data processing, large-scale database operations, and enterprise applications requiring massive RAM allocations, though it is less optimal for workloads dependent on high single-threaded clock speeds.
